draft.title: Strategic role of HRM
card: Human resource management (HRM) is the management of the people who work in a business. It covers finding, developing, rewarding and keeping staff.
A business sets goals, such as growing sales or improving service. These goals are its strategy.
HRM has a strategic role when it plans staffing around those goals. The aim is to have staff with the right skills and the motivation to meet them.
This is different from treating HR as only paperwork. A strategic approach asks what people the business will need to reach its goals.
draft.remember: Strategic HRM links the business's people to its goals.

a.q: Which action shows HRM playing a strategic role?
opts: Planning hiring and training to suit growth goals
Filing leave forms for staff as they are handed in
Hiring whoever applies first when a job becomes free
Keeping staff numbers the same from year to year
a.why: Strategic HRM plans people around the goals of the business. Filing leave forms is routine admin and does not link staff to goals. Hiring whoever applies first has no link to the skills the goals need.
a.clue: Look for the option that starts from the business's goals.

b.q: Priya's bakery chain in Perth plans to open a catering arm next year. Which HR step best fits a strategic role?
opts: Recruit and train staff in catering skills before the launch
Pay all current bakers the same as last year
Wait until the launch, then hire for any gaps that appear
Cut training costs so profit looks better this year
b.why: The step ties staff skills to a new goal before it starts. Waiting until gaps appear is reactive, so staff may not be ready to meet the goal. Cutting training works against the skills the goal needs.
b.clue: Which step prepares staff for a goal that has not started yet?

a.best: Planning hiring and training to suit growth goals

b.best: Recruit and train staff in catering skills before the launch

proposal.title: Strategic role of HRM
card: Human resource management (HRM) is the management of the people who work in a business. It covers finding, developing, rewarding and keeping staff.

proposal.remember: Strategic HRM plans the business's people around where the business is heading.

a.q: Which action shows HRM playing a strategic role?
opts: Planning hiring and training to suit the firm's growth plans
Filing staff leave forms promptly as they are handed in
Hiring whoever applies first when a job becomes free
Keeping staff numbers steady to make planning simpler
a.why: Strategic HRM plans people around the strategy and goals of the business. Keeping staff numbers steady sounds planned, but it is about convenience and is not tied to what the business needs. Filing forms and hiring the first applicant only react to events.
a.clue: Does the action depend on where the business is heading?

b.q: Priya's bakery chain in Perth plans to open a catering arm next year. Which HR step best fits a strategic role?
opts: Train staff in catering skills ahead of the launch
Keep all bakers on the same pay and duties as last year
Wait until the launch, then hire to fill any gaps
Cut training spending so this year's profit looks better
b.why: Training staff ahead of the launch lines their skills up with the new plan, so they are ready to meet the goal. Waiting to fill gaps is reactive, so staff may lack the skills when they are needed. Cutting training works against the skills the plan needs.
b.clue: A strategic approach looks ahead rather than reacting.
